identificationModule.briefTitle: Study Evaluating Preference, Satisfaction and Ease of Use of Inhalers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Diagnosed Patients
identificationModule.officialTitle: Study Evaluating Preference, Satisfaction and Ease of Use of Inhalers in COPD Diagnosed Patients

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Preference study: Genuair vs HandiHaler inhalers in COPD patients.

interventions.name: Genuair® (Almirall S.A.)
interventions.description: Inhaler with only placebo, once daily, 14 days

interventions.name: HandiHaler® (Boehringer Ingelheim's)
interventions.description: Inhaler with only placebo, once daily, 14 days

primaryOutcomes.measure: Percentage of Patients Who Prefer Genuair Device Versus Handihaler Device at Visit 2
primaryOutcomes.description: Patients will be asked to answer which device they prefer after 2 weeks of daily practice (visit 2)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Mean Overall Satisfaction With Genuair and Handihaler at Visit 2
secondaryOutcomes.description: The patient will be asked to rate the overall satisfaction with each device using a Likert-type scale (from 1 \[very dissatisfied\] to 5 \[very satisfied\]) after 2 weeks of daily practice (visit 2)

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Percentage of Patients Making at Least 1 Critical Error Using the Genuair and Handihaler Devices at Visit 2
secondaryOutcomes.description:
The correct use of devices will be assessed measuring the errors made by patients when using each device after 2 weeks of daily practice (visit 2).

Critical error is defined as the one that compromise the potential benefit of the treatment such as those that impede drug deposition in the lungs or delivery of sufficient dose.

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult male or female patients aged ≥ 40 with stable COPD
* Naïve patients to the use of study inhalers
* Patients agreeing on participating and signing the Informed Consent Form

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with other clinically significant disease, particularly body malformations or diseases affecting coordination and/or motor system
* Patients unable to read product package instructions and answer patient reported questionnaires

participantFlowModule.recruitmentDetails: This study was conducted 4 centres, 2 in The Netherlands and 2 in Germany. The first patient was screened in June 2011 and the last patient visit was in January 2012.

groups.title: Placebo Genuair (Daily) Then Placebo HandiHaler (Daily)
groups.description: Each morning, patients used the Genuair® (Almirall S.A.) inhaler containing placebo followed by the HandiHaler® (Boehringer Ingelheim) inhaler containing placebo. The study period consisted of 1 period of 14 days.

groups.title: Placebo HandiHaler (Daily) Then Placebo Genuair (Daily)
groups.description: Each morning, patients used the HandiHaler® (Boehringer Ingelheim) inhaler containing placebo followed by the Genuair® (Almirall S.A.) inhaler containing placebo. The study period consisted of 1 period of 14 days.

achievements.comment: 1 patient used Handihaler® once only, Genuair® zero times, \& was excluded from the safety population

groups.title: Overall Study Safety Population
groups.description: All patients randomized into the study excluding 1 patient who used Handihaler® once only, Genuair® zero times, \& was excluded from the safety population

outcomeMeasures.title: Percentage of Patients Who Prefer Genuair Device Versus Handihaler Device at Visit 2
outcomeMeasures.description: Patients will be asked to answer which device they prefer after 2 weeks of daily practice (visit 2)
outcomeMeasures.populationDescription: ITT: all randomized patients who used both devices at least once and expressed a preference for either or neither inhaler. 24 patients (12 each arm) received the incorrect treatment allocation and were excluded from the ITT population. Missing data was handled via the observed cases approach.

outcomeMeasures.populationDescription: ITT: all randomized patients who used both devices at least once and expressed a preference for either or neither inhaler. 24 patients from the safety population (12 each arm) received the incorrect treatment allocation and were excluded from the ITT population. Missing data were handled via the observed cases approach.
